mcqs.question: A solid is formed by attaching a right circular cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm to one face of a cube of side 6 cm. The cylinder’s base exactly coincides with the cube face. What is the total surface area of the composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cube SA = 6×6² = 216 cm². One face (36 cm²) is hidden, so exposed cube area = 216‑36 = 180 cm². Cylinder curved SA = 2πrh = 2π·3·10 = 60π. Only the top base is exposed (πr² = 9π). Total SA = 180 + 60π + 9π = 180 + 78π cm². Options B, C, D either forget to subtract the hidden face or omit the top base, leading to over‑ or under‑counting.

mcqs.question: A solid consists of a right circular cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 12 cm with a hemisphere of the same radius placed on top of it. What is the volume of the composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cylinder volume = πr²h = π·25·12 = 300π cm³. Hemisphere volume = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π·125 = (250/3)π cm³. Adding gives 300π + (250/3)π = (900/3 + 250/3)π = (1150/3)π cm³. The other options miss either the hemisphere part or use incorrect coefficients.

mcqs.learning_point: Avoid counting hidden surfaces when finding exposed area
mcqs.question:
Two composite solids are formed as follows:
(i) A cube of side 8 cm with a square pyramid (base 8 cm, height 6 cm) attached to one face.
(ii) The same cube with a right circular cone (base radius 4 cm, height 6 cm) attached to one face (base coincides with the cube face).
Which statement correctly compares their total exposed surface areas?

options.A: Solid (i) has a larger exposed surface area than solid (ii).
options.B: Solid (ii) has a larger exposed surface area than solid (i).
options.C: Both solids have the same exposed surface area.
options.D: The exposed surface areas cannot be compared with the given information.

mcqs.answer: Solid (i) has a larger exposed surface area than solid (ii).
mcqs.explanation:
For solid (i): Cube SA = 6·64 = 384 cm². Subtract the hidden face (64 cm²) → 320 cm². Pyramid lateral area = ½·perimeter·slant = ½·32·√(4²+6²)=16·√52≈115.4 cm². Total = 320 + 115.4 ≈ 435.4 cm².
For solid (ii): Cube exposed area = 320 cm² (same subtraction). Cone lateral area = πrl = π·4·√(4²+6²)=4π·√52≈90.5 cm². Total ≈ 410.5 cm². Hence solid (i) is larger. Options B‑D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: A water tank is made by joining a rectangular cuboid of dimensions 10 m × 8 m × 6 m with a hemispherical dome of radius 4 m on top of the 10 m × 8 m face. The bottom of the cuboid rests on the ground and the face on which the dome sits is not painted. What is the total surface area that needs painting?
mcqs.explanation: Cuboid total SA = 2(lw+lh+wh) = 2(80+60+48)=376 m². The bottom (80 m²) and the top face (80 m²) are not painted, leaving 376‑160 = 216 m² of exposed cuboid surface. The dome is a hemisphere; its curved area = 2πr² = 2π·16 = 32π m². Adding gives 216 + 32π m². Options B‑D either add the hidden faces or use half the dome area, which is incorrect.

mcqs.question: A solid is formed by attaching a right circular cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm to one face of a rectangular prism of dimensions 6 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm. Which list correctly identifies the component solids of this composite shape?
mcqs.explanation: The description mentions a right circular cone and a rectangular prism (also called a cuboid). Hence the components are a cone and a rectangular prism. The other options name different solids that are not present.

mcqs.question: A composite solid consists of a cube of side 6 cm with a square‑based pyramid (base side 6 cm, height 5 cm) attached to its top face. What is the total exposed surface area?
mcqs.explanation: Cube SA = 6·36 = 216 cm². The top face (36 cm²) is hidden, leaving 180 cm². Pyramid slant height = √(3²+5²)=√34≈5.83 cm. Lateral area = ½·perimeter·slant = ½·24·5.83 = 12·5.83≈69.96 cm². Total exposed SA = 180 + 69.96 ≈ 250 cm². Options B‑D miss either the hidden face subtraction or the pyramid’s lateral area.

mcqs.question: A solid is formed by placing a cone (radius 2 cm, height 5 cm) on top of a cylinder (same base radius 2 cm, height 10 cm). What is the volume of the resulting composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cylinder volume = πr²h = π·4·10 = 40π cm³. Cone volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π·4·5 = (20/3)π cm³. Adding gives 40π + (20/3)π = (120/3 + 20/3)π = (140/3)π cm³. The other options either omit one part or use wrong coefficients.

mcqs.learning_point: Avoid counting hidden surfaces when finding exposed area
mcqs.question: A square‑based right pyramid (base side 10 cm, slant height 13 cm) is fixed on one face of a cube of side 10 cm. What is the total exposed surface area of the composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cube SA = 6·100 = 600 cm². One face (100 cm²) is hidden, leaving 500 cm². Pyramid lateral area = ½·perimeter·slant = ½·40·13 = 20·13 = 260 cm². Total exposed SA = 500 + 260 = 760 cm². Options B‑D either forget to subtract the hidden face or mis‑calculate the lateral area.
